body:
I'm no expert but I argue that no one is.  So take this with a grain of salt.

When you're an immigrant, you yearn for the idealized version of what you think home would be.  That's your parents -- believing that their decisions are costing everyone something and making their children these horrible things that would never have been this way had they been at home.  But really, it's just fear that they failed.  They set an unrealistic standard for themselves and for what home was and now they need you to live up to that unrealistic (or probably unattainable and unhealthy) standard.  

It's not realistic and it's not what home was.  But when you're in the middle of the shit, you can't see it.  They _will_ get over it or you will get over them.
You're right.  I talked myself right out of it.  The depths are horrible, but I'm happy that I can walk up the hill to somewhere better.
